preregistered: 2026-09-22, written before any residual was computed; instants are fixed and not tuned afterwards
design: 24 UTC instants stratified by epoch over the DE440s span (1850-2150), non-round minutes so no instant sits on a midnight/noon phase of any table; two deliberately include a Sun-adjacent body (2012-05-21 Moon near the Sun the day after an annular eclipse; 2020-12-21 Jupiter-Saturn great conjunction) so solar deflection and outer-planet centre effects are exercised; 2148-12-30 sits near the end of pack coverage.
clock: For configurations a, b, d, e the clock is held fixed: TT = UT + Swiss deltat_ex(jd_ut, FLG_SWIEPH) as returned by pyswisseph 2.10.03 with the DE441-based .se1 files. Horizons is queried at that TT with TIME_TYPE=TT. The shipped engine (c) is run twice: at the UTC instant with its own astronomy-engine Delta-T (c-raw, what production does) and at a UTC shifted by (deltaT_swiss - deltaT_ae) so its TT equals the fixed clock (c-pinned).

configurations.a: Swiss 2.10.03 .se1 (sepl_18/semo_18, header: based on JPL DE441), FLG_SWIEPH|FLG_SPEED, apparent geocentric ecliptic of date tropical
configurations.a_centre: same plus FLG_CENTER_BODY with sepm9599..sepm9999 planet-centre files
configurations.b: Swiss 2.10.03 reading JPL DE440 (linux_p1550p2650.440, sha256 29915576...) via FLG_JPLEPH|FLG_SPEED
configurations.d_pack: precision-alpha apparent(body, ttDays, CORRECTED) over D.v2.zeph (1.66 MiB pack compiled from de440s.bsp by another auditor)
configurations.d_kernel: precision-alpha Reducer over SpkBackend(de440s.bsp) with CORRECTED (uncompressed)
configurations.e: JPL Horizons API, CENTER=500@399, QUANTITIES=31, TIME_TYPE=TT, TLIST of the 24 TT instants, one request per body (10 requests)
